Getting Started

Install

npm i -g serve-my-md

Run

serve-my-md --directory .

The CLI scans markdown files in the target directory and generates a static website there.

What gets read automatically

  • smm.config.json at docs root (if present)
  • .smmignore at docs root (if present)
  • fallback to built-in defaults when these files are missing

Important index.md behavior

  • index.md is the landing page for its directory.
  • index is never included in the pathname.
  • Internally, an index.md entry is treated as "" (empty string) in route tree naming.

Example:

docs/
  index.md
  guides/
    index.md
    install.md

Routes:

  • /
  • /guides
  • /guides/install

Coming soon

  • dev command support is planned.

CLI Reference

Main command

  • serve-my-md: build a static docs website from markdown files.

Options

  • -d, --directory <path>: docs root path (default .).
  • -i, --interactive: prompt for docs root.

Behavior notes discovered from source

  • Loads config from ./smm.config.json relative to target directory.
  • Loads ignore rules from ./.smmignore relative to target directory.
  • If publicPath is set in config, copies that directory into app public assets before build.
  • Uses markdown-it with task lists and footnotes plugins enabled.
  • Generates OG/meta/font tags in HTML from config values.

Runtime/navigation behaviors (from web app usage)

  • Markdown links with non-HTTP hrefs are intercepted and navigated client-side.
  • Intent-based link preloading is used for faster navigation.
  • Keyboard shortcuts include:
    • Search: Ctrl+Shift+F
    • Next page: Alt+Enter
    • Previous page: Alt+Shift+Enter
  • Search returns matches in current page and across other pages.

Test-only option

  • --skip-build exists only in vitest mode, not in normal CLI usage.

Routing and Sidebar Patterns

index.md is landing page

  • index.md represents the landing page for its directory.
  • index is not part of URL pathnames.
  • In nested name handling, index.md maps to "" (empty string).

Grouping directories with parentheses

Directory names wrapped in () act as grouping buckets:

  • shown as grouped section in sidebar
  • skipped from route pathname segments
  • should not contain index.md

This is useful when you want visual grouping without adding extra URL segments.

Example:

docs/
  (Guides)/
    setup.md

Route:

  • /setup

Regular directories (without parentheses)

  • appear as collapsible sidebar containers
  • can have index.md and be clickable landing pages
  • are included in pathname segments of child files

Example:

docs/
  guides/
    index.md
    setup.md

Routes:

  • /guides
  • /guides/setup

Ordered filenames with index prefixes

If you use names like:

  • 1. blahblah.md
  • 2. blhalbhablah.md

and set trimming in config (see config docs), names can be ordered while emitted as clean paths.

Slug generation rules

Route path segments are normalized by the CLI:

  • converted to lowercase
  • spaces/underscores become -
  • punctuation like .,;"'\\:<>?!` is removed
  • group directory names like (Group) are excluded from final pathname

smm.config.json

Place smm.config.json at docs root.

Defaults are merged with your overrides.

Default values come from the CLI's built-in config at cli/src/smm.config.json.

This is the complete schema:

export interface SmmConfig {
  rootTitle?: string;
  description?: string;
  markdownItOptions?: Record<string, any>;
  baseRoute?: string;
  publicPath?: string;
  defaultTheme?: string;
  favicon?: string;
  logo?: string;
  name?: string;
  showNameWithLogo?: boolean;
  og?: OpenGraph;
  sortRoutes?: boolean;
  trimIndexFromPath?: boolean;
  version?: string;
  fonts?: {
    title?: {
      name: string;
      url?: string;
    };
    body?: {
      name: string;
      url?: string;
    };
    mono?: {
      name: string;
      url?: string;
    };
  };
}

Read next:

  • Defaults and Options
  • Trim and Ordering

Defaults and Options

smm.config.json supports these useful options:

  • rootTitle: document title.
  • description: default description.
  • markdownItOptions: markdown-it constructor options.
  • baseRoute: route base prefix.
  • publicPath: directory to copy as public assets.
  • defaultTheme: initial theme.
  • favicon: favicon URL/path.
  • logo: logo URL/path.
  • name: brand/app name.
  • showNameWithLogo: show name near logo.
  • og: Open Graph tags object.
  • sortRoutes: sort routes tree.
  • trimIndexFromPath: trims filename numeric prefixes from route names.
  • version: docs/site version string.
  • fonts: title/body/mono font names and optional stylesheet URLs.

Default values used when user config is missing

{
  "rootTitle": "Serve My MD",
  "description": "A simple markdown to static site builder.",
  "baseRoute": "/",
  "defaultTheme": "dark",
  "markdownItOptions": {
    "html": true,
    "xhtmlOut": true,
    "breaks": true,
    "langPrefix": "language-",
    "linkify": true,
    "typographer": false
  },
  "favicon": "",
  "logo": "",
  "name": "Serve My MD",
  "showNameWithLogo": true,
  "sortRoutes": true,
  "trimIndexFromPath": false
}

Example:

{
  "rootTitle": "My Docs",
  "description": "Team documentation",
  "baseRoute": "/",
  "defaultTheme": "dark",
  "sortRoutes": true,
  "trimIndexFromPath": true,
  "publicPath": "public"
}

Trim and Ordering

Use numbered file names to force custom ordering:

  • 1. intro.md
  • 2. install.md

When trimIndexFromPath is true, the numeric prefixes are removed from emitted route names while order stays controlled by your naming.

Input files:

1. blahblah.md
2. blhalbhablah.md

Emitted routes:

  • /blahblah
  • /blhalbhablah

If trimIndexFromPath is false, or not present, then the emitted routes would be:

  • /1-blahblah
  • /2-blhalbhablah

If route sorting is enabled, routes are sorted lexicographically, with grouped (Name) directories ordered after regular names at the same level. Indexing can also be used for Grouper directories(directories whose names are enclosed within parenthesis) to determine their order.

.smmignore

Create .smmignore at docs root to skip paths during markdown traversal.

Rules are glob-like, processed top-to-bottom.

  • Lines starting with # are comments.
  • Empty lines are ignored.
  • Prefix with ! to un-ignore.

Example:

drafts/**
private/**
!private/keep.md

Paths are evaluated against traversal targets in the docs tree; ignored paths are skipped during route/content generation.

Examples

This section has practical structure and config examples.

Read next:

  • Structure Examples
  • Config Examples

Structure Examples

Group directory (not in pathname)

docs/
  (Category)/
    tos.md

Route: /tos

Normal directory with landing page

docs/
  features/
    index.md
    tea.md

Routes:

  • /features
  • /features/tea

Root landing page

docs/
  index.md
  about.md

Routes:

  • /
  • /about

Config Examples

Basic customization

{
  "rootTitle": "Company Docs",
  "description": "Internal knowledge base",
  "defaultTheme": "dark",
  "sortRoutes": true
}

Ordered file naming + trimmed paths

{
  "sortRoutes": true,
  "trimIndexFromPath": true
}

Public assets

{
  "publicPath": "public"
}

This copies public from docs root into build public assets, also ignores it for routes building.

Markdown and Rendering

The CLI uses markdown-it and includes:

  • footnotes support
  • task lists support

Code highlighting is enabled through Prism with language classes like language-js.

Useful notes:

  • linkify is enabled by default in config options.
  • fuzzyEmail linkification is disabled.
  • You can override markdown-it behavior via markdownItOptions in smm.config.json.

Additional rendering behavior from the web app:

  • Heading elements are assigned generated ids for anchor navigation.
  • Other extracted elements can receive internal labels for in-page search scroll targets.

Build Output and Assets

Build flow highlights:

  • markdown files are parsed into route/content JSON
  • generated data is written under web generated assets
  • static app is built and copied to target docs directory

Generated files consumed by the web app:

  • .generated/output.json: metadata and parsed route content
  • .generated/paths.json: nested tree used to render sidebar groups/collapsibles

If publicPath is configured and exists, that directory is copied as public assets before build.

If no smm.config.json or .smmignore exists, defaults are used automatically.
